name: Bruno Iksil

summary.text: Bruno Iksil was a trader in JPMorgan Chase's Chief Investment Office in London whose large synthetic credit index positions earned him the nickname 'the London Whale' when they lost more than $6 billion in 2012. In August 2013 he signed a non-prosecution agreement with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York in exchange for cooperation, and prosecutors instead charged his supervisor Javier Martin-Artajo and junior trader Julien Grout with scheming to inflate the marks on the portfolio. Prosecutors later dropped that case, saying they could no longer rely on Iksil's testimony.

facts.claim: In August 2013 Iksil signed a non-prosecution agreement with U.S. prosecutors that prevents him from being charged in exchange for his cooperation; press reports said the CFTC also agreed not to pursue civil charges against him.

facts.claim: In August 2013 the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York filed criminal charges against Javier Martin-Artajo, who oversaw trading strategy for the synthetic portfolio in the CIO's London office, and Julien Grout, a trader who worked for him, accusing them of scheming to inflate the value of position marks.

openQuestions: Site description of Iksil as 'the London Whale trader who built the massive CDX index positions': supported in general terms by press coverage; the Senate report body text was not read for the specific position details.
The exact date the charges against Martin-Artajo and Grout were dropped was not confirmed; the Gulf News report describes the case as about five years old, consistent with 2017.
No SEC or DOJ primary document naming Iksil was returned; the SDNY press release and SEC litigation release for the Martin-Artajo/Grout case should be located.
